newsitem.title: UK: Low sulphur under pressure on Euro fuel markets.
newsitem.headline: Low sulphur under pressure on Euro fuel markets.

text.p: European fuel markets made their habitual slow start to the week on Monday with poor bunker demand holding barges back and low sulphur physical cargoes having trouble rousing buyers, traders said.
High sulphur barge offers drifted $1 down to $83 a tonne on poor bunker demand, but no trades were seen.
"Its a typically dull start but everyone is looking to the swaps which are firmer for the month than today's physical so maybe we'll see some upside later," said one trader.
Opinions differed as to how much cracked Russian fuel was on the market.
Some saw a temporary shortage caused by a thin loading schedule in St. Petersburg in the first five days of June.

Buying interest in low sulphur cracked was very thin, with a northern German cargo failing to attract bids and other material about to emerge from the shadows. Prices were following swaps, which began to trail lower on Friday afternoon to $92.75/$93.50 for June.
In contrast low sulphur straight-run was perceived thinly supplied and numbers well supported at $106/$108 a tonne fob.
High sulphur cracked fuel was stronger in the Mediterranean on the back of sentiment and attempts at arbitrage plays.
"Med swaps are up the back of expectation of continued demand for arbitrage cargoes to take to the Far East or North America," said one trader, "but a lot of it is just hype."
June swaps in the Med were talked at $76/$77, with physical a dollar lower.
